Why so many maps still use red and green

A short history of traffic lights, stock tickers and the colors we keep choosing.

Red means stop and green means go. The pairing is older than the car, and it has spread to almost every dashboard, chart and status light on the web. For about one in twelve men, those two colors can look nearly the same.

Designers have options: add labels and patterns, use blue and orange, or check their work with a simulator. Readers have options too: tools that shift colors so that the difference returns. Read more about color-safe palettes.

Never rely on color alone to carry meaning.
